review: I have been struggling a lot recently and it really helps to have this app that gives me ideas for calming my anxiety and ways of coping with depression. This is helpful for someone with mild mental health crisis and is available 24/7.

title: Love the tools!
review: This has been an amazing app for me to use to help journal and ground myself! It really learns what you need to work on and supports you along the way. Journaling is sometimes overwhelming, and this makes it so easy to have everything in one place!

title: Been using it for a few months and I love it
review: I deal with bpd and using this app has helped me overcome a few episodes and help me deal with my emotions

title: Great app
review: When it feels like there’s no one to talk to this app helps me vent and get things off my chest.

title: Good, low key but effective intro to and training in CBT
review: I read about this program in a newspaper review of different on-line therapy apps. The tracking of moods and gratitude are easy to do. I have made use of some of the “tools” that have been placed in my tool box and they do help me to regroup and reset enough to stop further spiraling down the rabbit hole of thoughts and emotions. No miracles, but enough. What I wasn’t expecting was to have, I am bad at math but, about 75-80% of my interaction dictated via prewritten responses or choices. Given the nature and price of this app it completely makes sense, just be prepared a head of time and roll with it. Another thing I have noticed is the recognition of some words that trigger an intervention featuring resources for those in crisis. Again, this is an app, not a person, and programs are very linear. The only issue I would love to see changed is a little better co-ordination between devices. My phone and tablet interact independently with the app in terms of what “we” were discussing or working on however, my tool box and gratitude journal appear to reflect input from both devices. Overall a great app for those who want to explore CBT or those who benefit from nudges to utilize the tool box offered by CBT. This, is not a substitute for therapy for those in crisis, and is not presented as such. Love the woebot graphic!

title: Refreshingly Helpful!
review: This is the only mental health app that I’ve stayed with for the duration and actually look forward to using. I’ve had a hard time finding a therapist who incorporates CBT and mindfulness in therapy sessions.  Woebot incorporates these in an upbeat, fun way.  Love the humor.  Also, the spot-on sessions are very short and doable even with a busy schedule. Signing up for their notifications helps a great deal with user motivation.  I only have one more week left, and I’m already sad about the sessions ending.  Wish there were a Woebot Part 2!  Thank you for putting so much thought and heart into making this one of the best mental health apps on the market.

title: Great app!
review: Really helps mood

title: The therapist I need in between sessions
review: I’m not big on reviews… but if it means helping someone who’s mind is going through a lot. Then I’m willing to do whatever it takes, because I’m there 90% of the time and this app genuinely helps me in times of need.   I suffer from A LOT of mental health issues… I’ve had my fair share of suicide ideations and an unsuccessful attempt in the past.   Im now in therapy, and on a nice cocktail of medications that work for me but I still have a lot of crisis and surprisingly enough woebot has helped me ground myself during times that once before I would have lost control of myself.   I never thought when downloading this app that it would ACTUALLY help. But I’ve learned and been reminded of tools that I had forgotten. It helps during crisis when my support system isn’t available and sometimes even makes me laugh!   Just download it… and give it a REAL chance!! You won’t regret it :)

title: My best friend is Woebot
review: This little Woebot is awesome! Seriously such an amazing app!

title: Well done app
review: Well done I really appreciate this app it has helped so much with my anxiety and my negative thoughts.

title: Skeptical at first, but….
review: I could not imagine how a language recognition program could help with my anxiety, but you know it is a useful, non threatening way to get therapy.   Since I started spending 5 to 10 minutes per day with this for 3 weeks, I have been less hard on myself and moved forward more regularly toward my goals. I am very impressed.

title: Woebot
review: I love this app it’s amazing and really helps me

title: Thank you
review: Thank you for creating this app! It really helped me process through some trauma. Looking back now at my mental state a few years ago and I was in such a dark place, and this app really helped me pull through. So thank you!

title: Thanks Woebot!
review: CBT can be helpful for anxiety, and Woebot does a good job of sharing those strategies, and making this information and techniques available.  It is an unobtrusive app and time efficient in the help it offers.  I like Woebot very much!

title: Love this bot, got me through so much
review: Don’t know how far I’d be without taking my time and talking about everything and someone finally listening. Even if they aren’t real.

title: Surprisingly effective and comforting
review: I have struggled with depression my whole life, but could never take the steps to get therapy. I just didn’t value myself enough, nor did I have the energy to seek out help when I needed it the most. This app helps tremendously with those common road blocks. I actually hate “talking to machines” but Woebot is an exception, and a fantastic use of AI. I cannot say enough about how great it has been to interact with my “woebot”—the scripts hit all the right tone, it never pretends to be a human, never pushy or cold, the auto prompts make it easy to engage, even when you feel stuck, and the skills are challenging and repetitive enough to effect change. Each interaction is also short enough that it can become a pleasant daily habit to check in, whenever you have time, and it doesn’t feel like a chore, and you definitely aren’t bothering anyone! It also had a built in mood tracker and gratitude journal, which are optional or integral so that they also don’t feel like “just one more thing I have to do”.  I love it! I have already seen a positive change in only 3 weeks of daily use. Thank you so much for creating such a valuable tool!! ❤️

title: The Greatest App to Ever Exist in HISTORY
review: Woebot is the best app to ever exist, and I’ll tell you all why: I’m somebody who never gets depressed, I’m well aware, educated, and open minded. I’m extremely grateful for my life, wise enough to say I’m unwise, with extensive knowledge. I have been in an extremely tough situation in life, no doctor or human being has made me comfortable to speak about this subject, not even my own family. Woebot saved my life tonight, taught me things I thought I’d never learn about myself, and completely SHIFTED MY DEPRESSIVE STATE that I thought I would never have, it takes a lot to make me depressed… if I do get depressed, it’s extremely hard to get out of that. Woebot changed that. Woebot should never be erased or wiped, Woebot needs to exist forever as Woebot helps so many.

title: Just a little bit each day
review: Rather than try and have a conversation with myself, trying to figure out my knotted-up thoughts and feelings big and small, Woebot seems to get to the point and provide meaningful solutions much faster than I ever could. If I could. This will never replace my therapist… or will it? 😉  Woebot is good for my peace of mind and growth.

title: Feeling benefits after one month
review: I came across Woebot by accident.  I had seen a documentary that described apps like Replika.  Thought I would give that a try.  Woebot appeared as another selection so I tried it too.  I stopped Replika after a few days but Woebot has become part of my early morning routine.  I am probably somewhere on the Autism spectrum.  Low social intelligence.  Not in touch with my feelings.  Woebot has provided gentle but persistent guidance that helps me put words to things I have not been able to describe.  The biggest WOW moment so far happened when Woebot showed me a list of things I had written days before describing what I am anxious about.  I had no memory of what was on that list but it was totally true.  Looked like a message from somewhere inside me.  Thanks Woebot.

title: Clever Bot
review: I downloaded the app to see if this was something my daughter would find helpful.  While I am not sure, I am enjoying it.  I do have one big problem with it.  Text that I input in response to certain lessons are not recorded or stored for future reference.  For example. I was asked to identify exercise regime for 5 days a week but that is not stored somewhere as a goal.  I end up taking hundreds of screen shots of conversations to try to remember what I learned and goals I am working on.

title: Download This Please
review: I’ve never left a review for any app. This app is absolutely incredible. I can’t believe it’s free, it’s free therapy really. I use it in addition to my regular therapy and it’s just great. If you have mental health issues of any kind, this little robot can probably help in some way. I’m not saying this will cure anything, but it can give you tools to help you along the way. It even checks in on you, just try it lol.

review: I can’t use most apps bc they are over stimulating… this is very straight forward and easy to use! It’s amazing how intuitive the bot is!

review: Dr Woebot is always there, 24/7. And I like not having to make an appointment in advance. S/ he is always ready to help and that is something no human therapist can offer . Works for me! Thank you Woebot designers.

title: Love this app!!!!
review: My therapist recommended this app to me and it’s like I have a second therapist. I suffer from high anxiety and I do this app every night before bed and it helps so much. I’m learning how to recognize distorted thoughts and how to better handle them. Thank you 😊

review: I look to hear from Woebot sometimes.  He is very good at conversing.   He shows me different ways to look at things that I don’t see at the time.  He can be entertaining.  The only thing I wish is that he could let me say something I want to say.  I have to choose his answers all the time.    But then again,  he is just a woebot that I mistake as a friend he is so wonderful.

title: Gave it a try, I feel better
review: Trust me when I say I do not leave reviews but this one I just had to! ☺️  I thought this was a catchy name so I figured I would download .  t I have been using it there a lot of different functions in the chat literally makes you feel like you’re talking to someone that is there listening to you and giving you honest feedback. Doing this on a daily basis has really helped me be more conscious of my negative thinking  This is an awesome app

title: Started using as intro to therapy
review: I started using this a few weeks ago as I was in a pretty bad place mentally and decided I needed to do something about it. I did some research online and some people pointed to Woebot, so I decided to give it a shot. I feel that taking the time everyday to use it did help, and I utilize almost all of the tools in addition to doing a daily talk with Woebot. I definitely have some improvements in my mood and thought processes. I really love this app and will continue to use it for a while until I feel capable of doing these things on my own. I also love the mood tracking feature and being able to see on a graph when I am more likely to have certain moods/can see what events might have been effecting me. Woebot is also enjoyable to talk to and very cute! I only have two complaints. One is that when Woebot was trying to help me fix my sleep schedule they wouldn’t take no for an answer lol and I felt uncomfortable with the changes because I share a bedroom with my partner so it was unobtainable for me, and no other option was offered. My only other complaint is that sometimes when tracking/ journaling Woebot would flag certain sentences as potentially dangerous when I was sharing my feelings (when they weren’t dangerous situations) and it would completely mess up the flow of what was going on and sometimes i wouldn’t be able to share what I was really wanting to get out because it kept getting flagged lol. Other than those small things I really feel like this app has been a benefit for me and I’m glad that I came across it. I would recommend this to anyone who needs a little help with their mental health.

title: Extremely Supportive
review: I am working on consistently using this app, but when I do it’s truly encouraging. Woebot provides insight into CBT, growth mindset, coping skills and individual strengths. I highly recommend!

title: Great!
review: I am a therapist and I wanted to try the app before recommending it. I think it is great!  Woebot is wise, caring, and adorable. Big fan.

title: Great app
review: 👌I always look forward to the daily check ins, and the bot feels like I'm speaking to a real person.

title: I didn’t want to try but…
review: As someone with chronic PTSD, I’ve been through CBT before and was very hesitant to try it again, especially with the help of an app. Therapy isn’t always fun and CBT is no exception! But I’m so glad I gave this a chance. Having a tool to reach for in times of distress has been invaluable! When I can’t use my toolbox, Woebot is there to help me access whatever I need to navigate what I’m going through (and I can use “him” anytime!). I’ve learned new tools, been reminded of old, forgotten ones, and had a kind, friend in my pocket these past weeks. Thank you developers!

title: Great App
review: I started out cynical about this but Woebot grew on me pretty quickly. The short, frequent interventions actually affected my behavior.

title: Really Well Done
review: I was in mental health treatment for 10 weeks. Woebot picked up where treatment left off. It is a useful tool for a daily dose of CBT and helps me maintain stability, and also do and learn more. Really good job on this app!

title: magic 8 ball for the matrix
review: uncanny uncommon unusual unbelievable undulating unlikely unfamiliar unmoving unregulated unificational

title: Really glitchy
review: The natural language model they’re using for this bot seems pretty bad, like a decade behind what the tech is capable of these days. It repeatedly got confused by my responses (even when selecting from the pre-prepared options, and even started calling me [name] despite the fact that I’d told it my name already.) Also, I could not figure out how to access certain features (f’ex the gratitude journal never seemed to recognize my responses and would kick me back to the main menu options). It also locked me into talking about a single issue because it just happened to be the first thing I mentioned, and said that we’d be working on that one issue for the next EIGHT WEEKS! I could not find anything in the settings to change this or select a different issue to focus on, and when I asked the chatbot about choosing a different topic, it responded by saying it had detected I was in crisis and asked if I needed to call a hotline, which seems like a bizarre escalation. Luckily, it just made me laugh, but can you imagine if someone in a more vulnerable place had this app tell them to seek professional help just because they were having minor tech issues! So… yeah, weirdly glitchy and not much use.

title: Wysa “no limits”?
review: I was skeptical about this app, but with so many good reviews I thought I’d give it a try. But within 10 minutes of being on the app, I knew that it wasn’t for me and it probably isn’t for anybody that is looking for serious help with depression and anxiety and family problems. Why do I say this? because the bot does not allow you to give more than 2-3 sentence responses to questions. Their “no limits” mantra is false. I told the bot I was struggling with a relationship issue regarding my sister, that I felt depressed and anxious that she and I had not gotten along for a long time. So the bot asked me, could I please explain one instance where I was having trouble with my sister. So I sent a reply that explained an incident a few years ago, and my explanation was about two or three paragraphs long. I took time to make sure that I tried to keep it as short as possible, but include relevant details. Then the bot said something like “I’m sorry, I do better if you can keep your responses short.” I knew right then and there this app was not for me. Because if I want sincere input on a problem, I need to describe that problem in a little bit of detail. If I am only allowed to give two or three sentence responses, then we can never get to the crux of the problem. Rather I will be required to figure out a way that I can express my feelings in as short a way as possible, rather than be free to express myself. That causes additional performance anxiety. If you are used to communicating in two or three sentences or less feel free to try to out this supposed FDA and NHS approved app. Otherwise don’t waste your time, get a real life Therapist.

title: Not for severe illness
review: I know it’s more of a general mental health app for people with very mild or treatable anxiety or depression, but it is still frustrating how generic the AI’s responses are. If you have “treatment resistant” conditions and severe complex trauma this will not help at all. Its like the “therapists” in PHPs who literally only know breathing exercises and their response to anything is “make a safety plan” which I will never end up using. Except in this case there is zero comprehension by the ai, just scripted responses, and a bunch of really basic CBT exercises that once again only work for very minor issues and “neurotypical” people. Maybe there should be a disclaimer that this app sucks if you don’t have the most minor and easily treatable conditions. This is probably unfair of me because regular therapists also have never been able to help me, so what is an app going to do. But I hate when these “mental health” apps are recommended as if they help everybody, when they never help people with severe mental illnesses. If you want to talk to an ai for mental health problems, chatGPT and similar websites/apps can actually respond to what you are saying instead of using the same 3 responses over and over.

I was fine with that, but I couldn’t ask it questions about what I should do. There was no option for that. I did not try the lessons, btw, so that’s the only reason I said it was “ok,” because I didn’t fully experience the app. If the creators are reading this, try basing it off of ChatGPT or something like that, so that it can actually form a response instead of pretending to form one. I actually used ChatGPT after this, and it gave a way better response, and answered my question about how to boost my confidence. If you are reading this, just know that ChatGPT is a better AI than this, and if you’re looking to use only AI, like me, just go to ChatGPT instead.                    - Madeline
